Prior art: QEMU has mapped an ELF kernel instead of reading it since 4.2 (Stefano Garzarella, `816b9fe450`, [qemu-devel 2019-07-24](https://patchew.org/QEMU/20190724143105.307042-1-sgarzare@redhat.com/20190724143105.307042-3-sgarzare@redhat.com), 2019), so #698's first candidate, mapping the file, was already upstream; what was left is the copy into guest RAM, which any loader pays: Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor read each PT_LOAD straight into guest memory ([rust-vmm/linux-loader](https://github.com/rust-vmm/linux-loader)), one copy as QEMU's. A `pread` into guest RAM against the mapping's `memcpy` was no faster on a laptop (9-11 ms each, not nested), where half the copy was faulting in the destination's huge pages and half the copy itself.
